name: Bumper beam
summary: A strong bar hidden behind the plastic bumper cover. It takes the first hit in a collision.
whatItDoes: It spreads crash forces across the front of the car and into the crumple zones, and protects the radiator and lights in small knocks.
howItWorks: The beam is usually steel or aluminium and bolts to crash boxes on the ends of the main frame rails. Those boxes fold up in a controlled way in a low-speed impact, so they can be replaced without repairing the main structure.
failureSymptoms: The bumper cover sits unevenly after a knock
Radiator damage after a minor impact
safetyNotes: Parking sensors and driver-assistance radar often sit in or behind the bumper. They may need recalibrating after any repair.
Repair crash structures with approved parts only.
